findings.message: This is an instance fix, and it regresses the path it stopped covering. The old code encoded spaces in AZDO_PROJECT at the point of use, so it covered both the clone-URL value and the value from the fleet-azdo secret. The new code encodes spaces only inside entrypoint.sh's dev.azure.com regex branch and removes the encoding here. When the clone URL does not match that regex, AZDO_ORG and AZDO_PROJECT keep the secret's values, and nothing encodes them any more. The fix is to encode once at the point of use with a shared helper that percent-encodes every byte outside the unreserved set while leaving existing %XX sequences alone. Apply it to AZDO_ORG and AZDO_PROJECT at every URL site (draft-pr, specclaw-azdo-pr and specclaw-azdo-issue). Alternatively, normalise the secret-sourced values too. The same gap exists for other raw characters in a clone URL, such as raw non-ASCII or `?` and `#`, which still pass through unencoded.
findings.scenario: FLEET_REPO_URL is a form the regex rejects (for example a visualstudio.com URL) and the fleet-azdo secret has AZDO_PROJECT='My Project'. Before this commit, ensure_pr built .../My%20Project/_apis/... Now it builds .../My Project/_apis/... with a raw space, so the PR search request fails or is malformed, and ensure_pr returns 0 silently and creates no draft PR. The ac7 test table has no row for the secret-only path, so it stays green.
